answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards unseen to the box.
answers.evidence: Setup: shuffle each entire tier; use 1 I, 5 II, and all 4 III; return unused cards unseen.

answers.answer: Four-player human: start at 1 VP; put two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) next to the board; put three troops in a garrison and nine in supply; take 1 water. Three-player human: start at 0 VP; use the same Agent, troop, and water setup.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: Score track on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, third/Swordmaster next to board; three troops in garrison, nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed on that Reveal turn, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns are optional; once you take a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped; Resolve Reveal Effects; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before placing the Agent may pay the destination cost if gained before entry. Resources from the Agent card or destination effects cannot pay that same entry cost. One card chooses only one Agent icon and sends one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placement can grant resources for entry; placement costs are paid before resolving destination/card effects; one card can't send multiple Agents; no-icon cards only revealed.

answers.answer: On a Combat space you may deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison, for up to five total; the four already garrisoned do not increase the two-extra limit. At a non-Combat space, troops are not deployed by the ordinary deployment rule. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison first.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruit from supply into garrison; at a Combat space deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to a post where your Spy currently is, without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls a Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing your Agent and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both, though two different Spies can be used.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence is decided just after placement; same Spy cannot do both.

answers.answer: Strength is 2×2 for troops + 3 for the sandworm + 4 for swords = 11. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; if last unit removed strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit in Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent you acting again; the window closes when all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, return troops from the Conflict to supply, reset all Combat markers to 0, and return sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: a player is not required to pass just because they passed earlier; once all pass consecutively resolve. Cleanup returns troops, resets markers, and returns worms.

answers.answer: In four-player play, the two tied for first each take the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. In three-player play, the tied players each take the second reward; no other reward is given and nobody takes the card. A player at 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in a four-player game leaves remaining players competing for third; with three or fewer no other rewards; tie means nobody takes card; 0 strength gets no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards do not double. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice again for a second VP, so pay 6 spice for 2 VP if doubling that reward.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms doubles; control and battle icons excluded; optional reward cost may be paid a second time (example 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2).

answers.answer: After winning, take the Conflict card face up into your supply, then check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon may match any of the three icons in your supply, flipping that pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: win and take card, then check for a face-up Conflict or Objective match; must flip matching pair; Endgame wild can match any icon.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which stays even if Influence later falls below 4 and can be earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gets the Alliance and its 1 VP, which is retained only while holding it. Tying the Alliance holder does not take it; a challenger must rise above the holder (or take it through the stated holder-loses-Influence FAQ trigger).
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: distinct reversal rules at 2 and 4; tying current holder does not steal; rising above transfers.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion during your Reveal turn, before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split a source across purchases. After buying a Row card, refill the Row and you may immediately buy its replacement if affordable. Put acquired cards face up in your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal turn purchases; pool or split Persuasion; replace Row cards and replacement may be acquired; acquired card goes face up to discard.

answers.answer: At an unoccupied Maker space, add one spice during Makers to its accumulated bonus; visiting gains all bonus spice in addition to the chosen base effect. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are not spent. The Shield Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin while present; a worm is deployed directly to your Conflict quadrant, never a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms: all bonus spice is gained; stated Deep Desert/Hagga options and costs; hooks not universal/spent; wall protects three locations; worms go directly to Conflict.

answers.answer: At Recall, if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. First, players may resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare VP. Ties break by spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: end at end of round; Endgame Intrigues first; tiebreakers listed in order.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup exposes two face-up contracts and places the rest face down in the bank: with no Shaddam, shuffle 20 (18 in bank); with Shaddam, set aside two Sardaukar contracts, shuffle the remaining 18 (16 in bank), and keep the two reserved. Add four CHOAM Imperium cards and four CHOAM Intrigue cards. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are excluded from standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: two face-up; 20 or 18 shuffled depending on Shaddam; additional four cards per deck; 10 contrasting-back contracts are Rise of Ix compatibility only.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon takes an available face-up public contract and refills its offer from the bank if possible. If no public offers remain, gain 2 Solari; set-aside Sardaukar contracts do not prevent this fallback for other humans. Harvest completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown spice total that turn; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts and Completing contracts: public contract/refill, 2 Solari fallback, and the three named completion conditions.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait until a future turn because you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. On completion announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: contract for space already visited must wait; completion is announced, rewards gained, token flipped face down and left in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; First Player is the human whose Objective bears the marker; turn order is First Player, Rival, other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup: shared Rival, Ornithopter Objective, human First Player, order; Rival never takes a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of its specified type; if none exists, ignore placement; either way reveal another card and continue the turn. Ignore normal space costs/effects and apply only the Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy procedure; ignore ordinary space rules; reshuffle immediately on empty deck or Reshuffle.

answers.answer: For three or four players, omit Objective cards whose player-count marking does not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and give one face up to each player; the card marked First Player determines the first player. Shaddam may be chosen only when using CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5: Leaders may be chosen or random; omit mismatched Objectives and distribute face up; Shaddam only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if they run out. Troops are limited by the pieces in your supply, so you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource payments go back to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: tokens are not meant to be limited and substitutions are allowed; payments return to bank. Recruiting: no troops in supply means cannot recruit until some return.

answers.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top and place it face up atop the cards remaining from prior rounds, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, humans return Agents to Leaders, First Player passes clockwise (in 2P the Rival resets and First Player alternates between humans), then start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases and Round Start reveal then draw; Recall describes return of Agents and First Player procedure.

answers.answer: Yes. Board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be carried out in any order after placement. No: entry costs and requirements must be met before resolving those effects, so that visit's Influence cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs/requirements before effects; space and Agent-box effects may be in any order; Faction advance is among those effects.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost can normally be paid only once per turn; the exception is sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward. Most card/space effects are mandatory; 'may', optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are exceptions. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs: once per turn except doubled reward. FAQ: most effects mandatory; listed optional cases; Intrigue conditions and costs must be met.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spy in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement specifies an Agent-icon type, the post must be connected to a board space with that icon; otherwise you cannot place it.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: unoccupied post; recall one for no effect if supply empty; some effects specify an Agent icon connected to the post.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. You may use a Spy without a card for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence. You cannot recall the same Spy for both; two Spies may be used. Gather Intelligence is chosen immediately after placing the Agent, before space or card effects.
answers.evidence: Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; both recall effects can be without a card; same Spy cannot be used for both; timing given.

answers.answer: A location's controller gets its visit bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict places your Control marker and replaces an opponent's marker. The defensive troop comes from the controller's supply when that location's Conflict is revealed, without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: controller bonus on any visit, control marker replaces opponent; at Conflict reveal controller may deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player receives the third reward; the winner keeps first reward and the card, and no further rewards are given. A tie for third gets nothing. Three tied for first each receive the second reward; no other rewards are given and nobody takes the card.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and tie table: second-place tie, third-place tie, and three tied first outcomes.

answers.answer: In a normal three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive their printed rewards; third receives nothing. The same rank payment applies with a Rival as a participant in the two-human-plus-Rival game.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with two or three players first and second get rewards; ordinary third gets nothing; two humans plus Rival counts as three.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and only with at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separately from your deck; after resolving, put them face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. What happens when that deck is exhausted is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards: timing, separate face-down holding, and face-up discard after resolving. No deck-exhaustion rule is stated.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard comes from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. The trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you choose an Intrigue from your hand to trash. Secrets makes each opponent with four or more Intrigues give you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Trashing; Intrigue cards—Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: A trash effect may remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or instructed to trash itself. Whether trashing The Spice Must Flow reverses a VP is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Trashing: eligible locations, destinations, and optionality. The summary does not state a VP reversal for trashing this card.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once when you acquire the card. Reshuffle discard into a new deck when you cannot draw because the deck is empty. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle when deck empty; Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up and in play until Clean Up unless trashed. Fremen Bond works with one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: definition, reciprocal Bond activation, and Clean Up timing.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one placed this turn; it may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from Conflict to your garrison. Whether 'retreat any number' permits choosing zero is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat. The summary does not state a zero-count interpretation.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain-two-Influence icon requires both Influence to go to one chosen Faction; it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum with the specified Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance icon requires holding token; some effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied with opponents, the formerly tied opponent takes it; if several were tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence / FAQ Alliance loss: tied opponent receives on holder losing Influence; if several tied, holder chooses; return if nobody at 4+.

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not specify how a card drawn during Reveal is treated relative to Reveal effects, or the timing of a Plot Intrigue whose effect applies at Reveal.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says Reveal effects apply to just-revealed cards; it does not address newly drawn cards or the named Plot timing.

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not state whether a 'when you win a Conflict' Intrigue may be played after a tie for first or how an Intrigue gained as a reward affects that trigger.
answers.evidence: Combat and Intrigue timing are described generally, but the named card timing cases are not specified.

answers.answer: The listed final tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, then garrison troops. What happens if all remain tied and whether scores may exceed 12 are unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Scoring gives four ordered tiebreakers; no complete-tie outcome or 12-point cap rule is stated.

answers.answer: No. All contracts you hold for that same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement; you must have held them when sending the Agent. A board-space contract is another effect of the Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all same-space contracts with one placement; board-space contract resolves as another Agent-turn effect in any order.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts; only he may acquire them, and he may choose one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring. His Signet Ring restriction on deploying units applies immediately for the entire Agent turn, so the troop he recruits cannot deploy that turn.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup reserves contracts but they do not begin in his possession; only Shaddam may acquire. Shaddam's restriction applies immediately for entire turn.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica side begins face up. Whether Reverend Mother Jessica can act on the flip turn is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications give Feyd token placement/end and Lady Jessica starting side; no flip-turn action detail.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; it may trigger again after losing Influence and later moving up through 2, but moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: reaching 2 while passing, repeated upward reach, not downward; Favor triggers only when discarded from hand.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, is not a Combat space, always draws one card and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM or with exhausted public offers gain 2 Solari; otherwise take a face-up public contract and refill if possible. It gives no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, has no cost, is not Combat, gives 1 Emperor Influence (counted once) and the same contract-icon result; it automatically advances Emperor once because it is an Emperor Faction space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: contract spaces table and shared icon rule; faction status clarifies Accept Contract is non-Faction and Dutiful Service is Emperor.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, and controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, summon two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one sandworm. Both also give all accumulated bonus spice even when choosing worms. Hooks are not spent. The Shield Wall restriction still bars worms at its three protected Conflicts while it remains.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows and Sandworms / Sandworm Reward Doubling: costs and options; Maker spaces grant all bonus spice; hooks never spent; wall protection.

answers.answer: Both options require City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, and no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if lacking them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Sietch Tabr: requirement and both listed options.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari each visit, and is not a Combat space. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits grant 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 once anyone has one; each player may gain it only once. Take the third Agent from beside the board to your Leader; it is available that round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Swordmaster row; Rival rules note its Swordmaster also lowers human cost.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence; it is not Combat. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Privilege row; it is Landsraad, not a Faction space.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access; it costs 3 spice and requires 2+ Guild Influence; it is not Combat. Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, not necessarily the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops; paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access and is Combat; choose 0 or 1 spice, gaining 2 Solari or 4 Solari if you pay 1 spice; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, costs 5 spice, grants 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, costs 1 water, grants 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and may trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, costs 4 spice, grants 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, and Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, no cost, no Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent remains there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, no Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, no cost, no Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Assembly Hall, Espionage, and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not explain False Orders' requirements or effects, whether an opposing connected Spy is required, or Litany Against Fear's red box condition.
answers.evidence: The summary includes general Spy and card rules but no rulings for these named cards.

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not state Manipulate's removal, acquisition discount, or when an unacquired card leaves the game.
answers.evidence: No Manipulate card rule appears in the summary.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and its Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, 1 water, and score and Combat marker at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame and it competes to win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Endgame trigger description.

answers.answer: When its total of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water reaches the Rival's printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that value. It must spend Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water, using each type as needed before the next and keeping leftovers. Its new Agent is usable in the current round.
answers.evidence: Rival Swordmaster resource total and mandatory spending priority; take third Agent usable in current round.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends a set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP per set. It cannot combine a mixed total of seven resources for a VP.
answers.evidence: After Swordmaster: each exact resource set yields 1 VP.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by its leftmost priority icon. It gains the human-like VP at 2 Influence and Alliance VP, but not the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: gains/loses Influence VP and Alliances but no 4-Influence resource bonus; least Influence/tie-break; numbered icon meaning.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination card it selects only the destination matching current conditions; if that destination is occupied, reveal a new card rather than using the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: destination selection conditions and occupied result.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Newly recruited troops go to the Conflict at Combat spaces and to its garrison otherwise. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus is simply omitted if unmet; it never prevents Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop deployment rule and conditional bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: post priority, all occupied, third Spy trigger, and no Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival sends an Agent to Combat that turn, those troops deploy too. If a Place Spy card has no legal post, ignore the placement and reveal another Hagal card because it did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: Scheme-recruited troops join same-turn Combat deployment; Place Spy continues either way.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice. If it summons none, take base spice (2 or 4 respectively); without Hooks or when the Shield Wall protects the Conflict, it takes base spice. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: exact worm/base-spice choice and always collect bonus spice.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card and add its bottom swords to strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no deployed unit does not get the bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: beginning of Combat, unit condition, bottom swords, Reshuffle handling, then human window.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival gets normal placement rewards, can gain control and control bonuses, gets defensive troops from supply on reveal of a controlled location's Conflict, wins battle-icon VP normally, and doubles rewards if it has worms. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts: a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat rules: control, defensive troop, icons, worm doubling, optional VP, and contract handling.

answers.answer: During Reveal Effects, total Combat strength, announce it, and set the marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed during that turn. If above 20, flip to the +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength: timing for total/announce/set and over-20 marker handling.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns. Merely revealing Signet Ring does not activate it. Card text can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: second Leader ability activates when playing Signet Ring on Agent turn, not merely revealing; Overview says cards can override rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, usually as a cost for a card's effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate optional recall uses described in the Spy rules.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon definition and separate cardless Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence effects.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and excludes Intrigues unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon. Discarding: hand card, not Intrigue unless specified.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm reward doubling permits paying the cost a second time to gain an optional reward a second time; the example allows 2 Influence with the same Faction or two different Factions. A single free-choice gain-two-Influence effect is different: both must go to one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence section says a gain-two free-choice icon cannot split factions.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival's Signet Ring ability printed on its selected Rival card, not its Scheme. The Hagal Signet icon itself triggers it; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme table: distinct triggers and abilities.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon takes one token if the Rival lacks one and does nothing if it already has one. Shield Wall removal removes the Wall only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks or if already gone, it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, no cost, and is not Combat. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws one Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one Intrigue selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Secrets row; Intrigue Steal icon specifies 4+ and random selection.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, and is Combat. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice; its controller gets 1 spice. If the visitor also controls it, that player receives both visit effects.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Basin; guide notes visitor and controller effects both apply, even for same player.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds. Each player draws five cards after that reveal.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: reveal and place atop remaining cards, then each player draws five.

answers.answer: Each of the four Faction Influence tracks begins with one human cube on its bottom space; the four Alliance tokens begin on their marked Faction tracks, not with players. The Shield Wall token begins on the board below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on marked areas, Wall below Refinery, cubes on bottom spaces.

answers.answer: In 3–4 player play, the First Player starts and turns proceed clockwise; after a player Reveals, that player's turns are skipped while others continue. Player Turns end when all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and goes clockwise; an eligible player may play any number or pass.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections state order, end condition, priority, and any number of Intrigues.

answers.answer: The three steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, and Clean Up. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order; they need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists its three steps and permits effects in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place it face down to the left of the Leader. Omit CHOAM-marked cards; shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately and place both face down; deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row; put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, and Control markers start in the player's supply; one cube per Faction track starts at its bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6 and Initial card states: deck and shared decks/Row/Reserve; components in supply; Combat marker and Influence cubes.

answers.answer: Ordinarily acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or Prepare the Way / The Spice Must Flow from Reserve. Cost is shown at the card's top right. These purchases use Persuasion during your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: eligible Row/Reserve cards, top-right cost, Reveal-turn timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when a legal action exists. A Shield Wall detonation icon may remove the token; once removed, it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Spies section says placement/recall optional; Shield Wall section says may remove and cannot return.

answers.answer: The played card needs an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left icon, unless it has the Spy Agent icon and a Spy at a connected observation post. A connected Spy by itself does not let a card with only City icon go to Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon and your Spy is connected to Shipping, it can send an Agent there without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: matching icon required; connected Spy alone insufficient; Spy Agent icon allows connected space without recall.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement join available supply and may pay entry. You cannot use resources gained only after placement from the Agent card or destination to pay that entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before Agent placement can fund cost; post-placement destination/card grants cannot pay that same entry.

answers.answer: No. After both humans Reveal, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply; begin Combat only after both humans Revealed and the Rival used all Agents. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: in 2P skip revealed humans but continue Rival Agents until exhausted; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to that Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After Conflict rewards, reset all Combat markers to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start and Critical Locations: defensive troop on Conflict reveal; Combat cleanup resets all markers.

answers.answer: Take one card from your hand, play it face up in front of you, and send one of your Agents from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve its Agent box and the space effects; ignore the Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card in play or discard, or simply move an Agent already on the board; the Agent-turn rule requires a card from hand and an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand; send Agent from Leader; use Agent box; normal cleanup/recall rules.

answers.answer: The restriction already applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send the Agent. He cannot postpone it by resolving board effects first, so he cannot deploy units on that turn.
answers.evidence: Shaddam clarification: restriction takes effect immediately; general effect-order freedom cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: First, second, and third place each receive their printed rewards; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with four players ordinary first, second, third rewards; winner takes card and checks match.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: take a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from the discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draws from own deck; if empty shuffle discard and continue.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place its deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup: shuffle House Hagal near Rival, retaining 2P Reshuffle card.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: all Hooks in common bank; later acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If Combat Intrigue changes units or strength, adjust the marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Use the adjusted strength shown on the track to resolve Combat after the eligible players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Combat: adjust marker on Intrigue resolution; Reveal strength is not fixed; resolve using adjusted track after passes.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the common bank, not another player's supply. Payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: take gains from bank and return payments to it.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then expose two face up beneath the Landsraad Council; put the rest face down in the bank. Players do not choose or preset the offers/order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: shuffle standard contracts face down, flip two face up, put remainder face down in bank.

answers.answer: Before the contract shuffle, set aside both Sardaukar contracts for Shaddam's exclusive acquisition; they are not his starting possessions and only Shaddam may acquire them. Shuffle the other 18, expose two face up and put 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts separate.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: Shaddam reserves two; shuffle remaining 18 for two offers and 16 bank; reserved tokens are not in his possession; exclusive acquisition rule.
